question: Do original Coin Metrics public GitHub CSV snapshots from 2026-03-26 and 2026-05-24 contain materially different older Bitcoin MVRV, price, and capitalisation rows; how far back can repository commit lineage prove historical data availability?
tests: Confirm source SHA1 Git blobs with exact length-prefixed blob bytes, and SHA256 over full downloaded raw CSV
Reject duplicate dates, missing 'time' column, dates out of order or outside BTC history; record per-source first/last/rows
Compare only intersecting exact date strings and available metric columns; include separate missing/null/added counts, do not impute
Compare every exactly equal date using Decimal not floats; count unchanged, changed, added and removed, and record 10 largest absolute differences where both numeric (no model selection)
Separately count relevant points on 2012-06-03, 2018-11-18, 2021-04-11, 2024-01-07, 2026-03-20 if present; these are descriptive checks only
Report visible repository commits do not prove original as-of 2012-2025; commit clock attests snapshots only as of 2026; pre-2026 PIT flags must remain false
Archive full comparative report, study manifest and source SHA/byte metadata to private Cloudflare R2 with GET SHA readback; do not bulk republish Coin Metrics CSV
limitations: GitHub-reachable main ancestry does not prove lack of other archives or unpublished versions
A GitHub commit timestamp alone does not prove upstream metric computational/publication latency
Retrospective rows are not independent original historical real-time vintages
No threshold tuning, no PnL/forecast or OOS claim
guard: RESEARCH_ONLY; no Spot, Futures, NAV, P&L, capital, reserves, MASTER, Detector, trading limits, orders, or live price writeback.
